prompt: Before OpenTelemetry, what did moving to another monitoring vendor cost a team?

choices.text: Changing the load balancer in front of the services
choices.why: The balancer has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: Nothing, since every vendor already read the same format on the wire
choices.why: There was no shared format; that is what OTLP became.

choices.text: A new database for the traces
choices.why: Storage was the vendor's; the code was the cost.

choices.text: Rewriting the instrumentation in every service
choices.why: Right. The recording code was tied to the product that stored it.

prompt: Which of these is not part of OpenTelemetry?

choices.text: Agreed attribute names such as http.route
choices.why: Those are its semantic conventions.

choices.text: A store for traces
choices.why: Right. Storage and screens are Jaeger's, Tempo's or a vendor's.

choices.text: A protocol for sending telemetry, OTLP
choices.why: OTLP is its protocol.

choices.text: A Collector that receives, processes and forwards telemetry
choices.why: The Collector is one of its parts.

prompt: Every service could send spans straight to Jaeger. Why put a Collector between them?

choices.text: The Collector draws the trace pages
choices.why: Jaeger draws them.

choices.text: Jaeger refuses OTLP sent by an SDK
choices.why: Jaeger accepts OTLP; the lab just routes through the Collector.

choices.text: Without it, every request would wait for its spans to be stored
choices.why: The SDK already sends in the background, Collector or not.

choices.text: It is the one place that changes when the back end changes
choices.why: Right, and where sampling and attribute removal are set once.

prompt: What turns a trace's spans into a tree?

choices.text: The parent id each span carries
choices.why: Right. The root's is empty.

choices.text: The order the spans reach Jaeger in
choices.why: Spans arrive in any order; section 07 shows batches that mix them.

choices.text: The service name in each span's resource
choices.why: A service has many spans at many levels.

choices.text: Their start times, sorted by Jaeger
choices.why: Time orders siblings; it cannot say who is whose parent.

prompt: What does propagate.extract(self.headers) do in payments.py?

choices.text: Reads the caller's span from the header, so payments' span becomes its child
choices.why: Right. That is how a trace crosses a process.

choices.text: Copies the box office's spans into payments' memory
choices.why: Only an identity travels, never the other side's spans.

choices.text: Sends the finished span to the Collector
choices.why: The batch processor does that.

choices.text: Checks the request's card number
choices.why: It reads tracing context, nothing of the sale.

prompt: How does payments get into a container without a Dockerfile of its own?

choices.text: It uses the box office's image with another command
choices.why: Right: compose.yaml sets command to python payments.py.

choices.text: It is pulled as a ready image from a registry
choices.why: It is built from the same Dockerfile.

choices.text: It runs on the lab machine outside Docker
choices.why: It is a service in compose.yaml.

choices.text: Compose generates one
choices.why: Compose builds what it is given.

prompt: Why do the sale's spans nest under the request's span with no ids passed by hand?

choices.text: A span started inside another's with block becomes its child
choices.why: Right. The open span is the current one.

choices.text: Jaeger nests the spans that overlap in time when it draws the page
choices.why: Jaeger uses parent ids, not overlaps.

choices.text: They share the route as an attribute
choices.why: Attributes describe; they do not link.

choices.text: The tracer gives every span of one thread the same parent
choices.why: Then sign and charge would be siblings of the request.

prompt: Why does the sale call payments before opening its transaction?

choices.text: OpenTelemetry refuses a CLIENT span inside a database span
choices.why: Spans of any kind can nest.

choices.text: So the row's lock is not held during a slow call
choices.why: Right. Lesson 1 showed what a held lock costs at the hot row.

choices.text: The transaction would otherwise be read from the replica
choices.why: Writes go to the primary either way.

choices.text: Payments needs the seat number first
choices.why: It is sent no seat at all.

prompt: What would an instrumentation library for psycopg add?

choices.text: Spans inside PostgreSQL's own processes
choices.why: It wraps the client calls in the service.

choices.text: A replacement for the Collector inside the database
choices.why: It runs in the service, beside the SDK.

choices.text: Faster queries
choices.why: It records; it does not tune.

choices.text: A span per query, without code in each handler
choices.why: Right. Same kind of span as the hand-made ones.

prompt: In collector.yaml, what does the batch processor do?

choices.text: Writes a log line per span
choices.why: The debug exporter writes one per batch.

choices.text: Keeps one trace in ten
choices.why: That is sampling, section 10.

choices.text: Assembles the spans of each trace into a tree before forwarding it to Jaeger
choices.why: Jaeger builds the trees.

choices.text: Groups spans for up to a second before passing them on
choices.why: Right: fewer, bigger requests to Jaeger.

the batch span processor collects it

prompt: The team moves from Jaeger to a hosted tracing service. What changes?

choices.text: The traceparent header's format
choices.why: It is a W3C standard, vendor-free.

choices.text: The exporters in collector.yaml
choices.why: Right. The services keep sending OTLP to the Collector.

choices.text: Every span's name, to match the vendor's conventions
choices.why: Names follow OpenTelemetry's conventions, which vendors read.

choices.text: telemetry.py, in both services, and their images
choices.why: They send to the Collector, whose address stays.

prompt: In the first sale, charge started at 0.1 ms and payments' span at 14.7 ms. What was that gap?

choices.text: The UPDATE waiting for the row's lock
choices.why: The UPDATE came after the charge, at 54.4 ms.

choices.text: Payments charging the card
choices.why: That is payments' own 23.2 ms span.

choices.text: Connecting and sending: work neither service's spans cover
choices.why: Right. A minute later the same gap was 1.8 ms.

choices.text: The Collector holding the span for its batch
choices.why: Batching happens after spans end; it does not move their times.

prompt: The first sale took 68.6 ms and its charge 38.3 ms. What percentage of the sale was the charge? Round to a whole number.
The Collector's debug lines showed batches of 6 and 3 spans, while the sale's tree had 6. Why don't they line up?

choices.text: Each batch is one trace, and two traces were in flight
choices.why: Batches are not cut by trace.

choices.text: The debug exporter counts services instead of spans
choices.why: It prints both, as resource spans and spans.

choices.text: The Collector dropped three spans of the sale
choices.why: Jaeger had all six.

choices.text: A batch holds whatever spans arrived in its second
choices.why: Right. The Collector forwards spans; Jaeger assembles traces.

prompt: The read took 14.5 ms and its SELECT 13.9 ms. What does that tell you a histogram could not?

choices.text: That the query was nearly all of that one read
choices.why: Right: where one request's time went.

choices.text: That reads are fast at the 95th percentile
choices.why: That is what the histogram said.

choices.text: How many reads there were that minute
choices.why: A counter says that.

choices.text: That the replica lags behind the primary
choices.why: A query's duration says nothing of lag.

prompt: Traces stop at one service and start again as new ones after it. What is the likeliest cause?

choices.text: Jaeger's storage is full
choices.why: That loses spans, not the link between them.

choices.text: The Collector's batch timeout is too short
choices.why: Batching does not change ids.

choices.text: The two services use different languages
choices.why: The header is the same in every language.

choices.text: Something in between drops the traceparent header
choices.why: Right: a proxy, a queue or a hand-written client.

prompt: In 00-5bd86167ca0ed7a647e37c1ebe501aac-b78031cb62daec0c-03, the field b78031cb62daec0c is the ___ id.
A call arrives at payments with flags 00, the sampled bit off. What does payments do with its span?

choices.text: It records it, because payments makes its own decision with its own ratio
choices.why: Parent-based samplers follow the parent's decision.

choices.text: It refuses the request
choices.why: Sampling never affects the answer.

choices.text: It records it and starts a new trace
choices.why: It continues the caller's trace id.

choices.text: It does not record it, following the caller's decision
choices.why: Right, under the parent-based sampler. A trace is kept or dropped whole.

prompt: A client sent its own traceparent to the box office. Whose trace id did Jaeger file the sale under?

choices.text: The client's, 0af7651916cd43dd8448eb211c80319c
choices.why: Right. The box office continued the trace it was given.

choices.text: The one nginx adds to every request it forwards
choices.why: nginx is not instrumented here and adds nothing.

choices.text: A new one, generated by the box office
choices.why: It continues traces it receives.

choices.text: A new one, generated by payments
choices.why: Payments continues the box office's.

prompt: What joins a log line to its trace?

choices.text: The trace id written in the line
choices.why: Right. The same 32 digits Jaeger files it under.

choices.text: Its timestamp, matched against the span's start
choices.why: Hundreds of requests share a millisecond.

choices.text: The host name of the copy that wrote it
choices.why: One copy serves many requests.

choices.text: The route and the status, which identify one request
choices.why: Thousands of requests share a route and a status.

prompt: What is an exemplar?

choices.text: A sample trace Jaeger keeps for each operation
choices.why: Exemplars live with metrics.

choices.text: A log line copied into a span as an event
choices.why: That is a span event.

choices.text: The first request after a restart
choices.why: Not a term here.

choices.text: A trace id attached to one observation of a histogram
choices.why: Right: from a slow percentile to one slow request.

prompt: Why does head sampling keep or drop a trace whole, rather than some of its spans?

choices.text: Jaeger refuses incomplete traces
choices.why: It stores whatever spans arrive.

choices.text: Later services read the decision in traceparent's flags
choices.why: Right. Half a trace is a tree with holes.

choices.text: Each span is sampled with the same random number
choices.why: The decision is made once, by the first service.

choices.text: The Collector drops the rest of a trace once it sees a gap
choices.why: The Collector here does not sample at all.

prompt: With parentbased_traceidratio at 0.1, about how many of 200 reads should be traced?
What does tail sampling need that head sampling does not?

choices.text: Every span of a trace at one Collector, held until it decides
choices.why: Right: memory, and routing by trace id.

choices.text: A sampler in every service
choices.why: Head sampling is the one in the services.

choices.text: A ratio below 1%
choices.why: Its policies are about errors and latency.

choices.text: A W3C header of its own

prompt: Traces are sampled at 1%. What happens to the request counter of lesson 7?

choices.text: It counts one request in a hundred
choices.why: Metrics are not sampled.

choices.text: It stops being updated until the sampler is turned off again
choices.why: The sampler knows nothing of metrics.

choices.why: Right. Sampling applies to traces, not to metrics.

choices.text: It counts the traced ones twice
choices.why: Tracing and counting are separate.

choices.text: At the Collector's batch size
choices.why: Batching does not slow a request.

choices.text: At the request counter

choices.text: At payments' span again, over many more samples than before
